get.description:
The authorization endpoint

Stores the authorization request in the session and sends the user to the login page,
or straight on to finishing the authorization when they are signed in already and the
login is recent enough for `prompt` and `max_age`. With `prompt=none` the user never
sees the login page, the client gets `login_required` instead.

An unknown client or `redirect_uri` sends the user to the error page and never to the
client. RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1: "the authorization server SHOULD inform the resource owner
of the error and MUST NOT automatically redirect the user-agent to the invalid
redirection URI." Every other error goes back to the client.

Seconds since the last login, beyond that the login page is shown again
Value the ID token echoes, binding it to this request
Space separated: "none" fails instead of showing the login page, "login" forces the login page, "consent" and "select_account" are ignored
Where to send the user with the authorization code
Only "query" is supported
Only "code" is supported
Space separated scopes the client requests
Opaque value returned to the client unchanged

get.description:
Issue the authorization code for the pending authorization request and redirect to the client

Sends the user back to the login page when they are not signed in yet or their login is
too old for the request (`login_required` with `prompt=none`), and to the error page
when this session has no pending request with that id. An account that is no club
member, or no longer exists, gets `access_denied`.

post.summary: Exchange an authorization code for an ID token and an access token
post.description:
Exchange an authorization code for an ID token and an access token

The client authenticates with `client_secret_basic` or `client_secret_post`
(RFC 6749 §2.3.1). Errors are RFC 6749 §5.2 error objects. Every response carries
`Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache` (RFC 6749 §5.1).

A code is redeemed once. RFC 6749 §4.1.2: "The client MUST NOT use the authorization
code more than once. If an authorization code is used more than once, the
authorization server MUST deny the request". A row lock serializes concurrent
redemptions.

The `redirect_uri` has to equal the one of the authorization request exactly, compared
as a string like the authorization endpoint does.

RFC 9700 §2.1.1: "a token request containing a code_verifier parameter is accepted
only if a code_challenge parameter was present in the authorization request"

post.summary: Sign in with username (or email) and password
post.description:
Sign in with username (or email) and password

An unknown username and a wrong password fail alike, so the response does not tell
which usernames exist. On success the session gets a new id, so an id planted or seen
before the login does not become a signed in session (session fixation).
